subject: Cloud marketplace fee allocation — carveout & liability language for addendum
messages:
From: Katy Barnes <katy.barnes@acme-cloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify marketplace fee allocation and pass-through carveouts

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the call earlier this week. Our procurement team asked us to get clarity on how Redwood intends to handle marketplace-related pass-throughs (platform fees, third-party taxes like VAT/GST, and any marketplace surcharge). The marketplace (Acme Marketplace) will bill our customers directly and they will remit a net amount to Redwood; however their platform also collects and remits certain taxes and charges at the point of sale.

Two asks from procurement:
- Can Redwood accept a carveout for marketplace-levied taxes/fees so Redwood is not held liable for those taxes when the marketplace invoices the end-customer?
- If not, what alternative language can we add to the addendum so liability and fee allocation are explicit (MSA + Order Form + Partner Paper)?

We are timeboxed here — the customer hopes to list next month. Please send your redlines or a short proposal by Tuesday (9/22). Happy to set a 30m call if helpful.

Thanks,
Katy Barnes
Head of GTM Partnerships | Acme Cloud
katy.barnes@acme-cloud.com

---
Attachment: Acme_Marketplace_Terms.pdf (reference only)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Katy Barnes <katy.barnes@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace fee allocation and pass-through carveouts

Katy —

Appreciate the context. I've attached an initial redline for the Marketplace Addendum that attempts to keep the customer experience intact while limiting Redwood's exposure on third‑party marketplace charges. High-level summary of the suggested changes:

- Explicit carveout for taxes/fees collected and remitted by the marketplace: proposed language in Section 2.a of the addendum clarifies that any taxes or platform fees collected directly by the marketplace from end customers are the responsibility of the marketplace and not billed back to Redwood.
- Order Form mapping: add a short clause to the Order Form so it options whether the customer was billed directly by marketplace vs. Redwood (so downstream accounting/commission can be determined).
- Indemnity/limitation: recommend limiting Redwood's indemnity to claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct and capping liability for marketplace-related claims to the aggregate fees Redwood actually received under the affected Order Form in the prior 12 months.
- Operational ask: if marketplace invoices customers directly, we need monthly remittance detail (invoice-level) from Acme for reconciliation — Marcus, can your team confirm workable fields?

I'm not prescribing final legal language yet; Kimberly, please confirm whether the carveout and 12‑month cap are acceptable. Marcus, can you review the reconciliation requirement and the fee-routing notes I added (see fee-flow diagram attached)?

If this looks reasonable to Acme, we can iterate quickly and route the final doc through DocuSign. I can host a 30m sync on Tue 9/22 at 10:00 PT if that works.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Partner Partnerships | Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
Mobile: (415) 555-0123

---
Attachment: ACME_Redwood_Marketplace_Addendum_v1_redlines.docx

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Katy Barnes <katy.barnes@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace fee allocation and pass-through carveouts

Soojin / Katy —

Thanks for the redline, Soojin. I reviewed and provided focused edits to reduce Redwood's exposure while keeping the commercial intent intact. Key legal positions I propose (see attached redlined file):

1) MSA/Order Form integration: add a connector clause that the marketplace addendum amends only the Order Form and not the MSA's core liability provisions except as expressly stated. This prevents an unintended expansion of obligations.

2) Taxes & fees carveout: change the carveout to read that Redwood is not responsible for taxes or platform fees "originating from charges imposed and collected by the marketplace directly from the End Customer." That precise phrasing prevents gamesmanship where a marketplace labels a fee differently.

3) Indemnity and liability cap: propose Redwood's indemnity remains limited to claims arising from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, and for marketplace-originated claims the liability cap should be the lesser of (a) fees paid to Redwood under the Order Form in the prior 12 months or (b) $250,000. This provides a fixed upper bound for tail risk.

4) Audit / reconciliation: require the marketplace to provide invoice‑level remittance reports monthly and allow Redwood a one‑time, narrowly scoped audit right (remote, 30 days notice) limited to fee flows related to Redwood listings.

Two operational questions for Acme: (i) will the marketplace provide invoice-level tax breakdowns (taxable amount, tax type, jurisdiction), and (ii) can procurement confirm that the marketplace contract obligates them to remit those details to sellers?

If Acme agrees, I'll finalize redlines and produce a clean execution copy for signature.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

---
Attachment: ACME_Marketplace_Addendum_v1_redlines_kp.docx

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Katy Barnes <katy.barnes@acme-cloud.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace fee allocation and pass-through carveouts

Team / Katy —

From a finance/ops perspective I have two primary asks before we sign:

1) Reconciliation fields: the remittance file needs (at minimum) -- marketplace invoice id, end-customer name, Redwood order-form id, gross amount charged, marketplace fees, taxes (broken out by jurisdiction), net remitted to Redwood. Without these we can't tie payments to invoices.

2) Commission / revenue recognition: if the marketplace invoices customers and remits net to Redwood, we need a monthly statement and supporting invoices to support revenue recognition and tax filings. If Acme can send a sample remittance file format (CSV or SFTP drop), that will speed up integration.

Operational note: if the marketplace will net fees and taxes before remitting, Redwood may require a short monthly reconciliation workflow (we can automate), but we also need to preserve the option to request a one‑time deeper analysis if anomalies exceed a tolerance threshold.

I've attached a simple fee-flow template and diagram to show what fields we'd expect. Marcus Lin
Director, Finance Operations | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

---
Attachment: fee-flow-ops.xlsx; fee-flow-diagram.png

From: Katy Barnes <katy.barnes@acme-cloud.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@acme-cloud.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify marketplace fee allocation and pass-through carveouts

Soojin / Kimberly / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear set of edits. Procurement confirms the marketplace invoices customers directly and Acme Marketplace will provide monthly remittance reports including tax breakdowns — they confirmed this in their onboarding docs.

We are comfortable with the 12‑month fees cap, but our finance team asked whether we can strike the fixed $250,000 number and instead set the cap solely to the fees paid to Redwood in the prior 12 months (Acme is being conservative on liability as well). If Redwood requires a minimum cap for internal risk tolerance, let us know what number you'd propose and we can escalate HQ.

Next steps: please produce a clean execution copy reflecting Kimberly's edits and the agreed reconciliation requirements. We'll review internally and route for signature via DocuSign. If you can get the DocuSign link over by EOD we can aim to sign before the end of the week.

Best,
Katy Barnes
Head of GTM Partnerships | Acme Cloud
katy.barnes@acme-cloud.com
